mcp.evidence_snippet: All DealCloud MCP tools are currently read-only and do not create, update, or delete data.

notes: Two auth paths: OAuth2 client_credentials (SDK + token endpoint, scope=publish for Publications) and a user-level API key enabled from Profile. MCP is read-only but REST is full CRUD, so buildability differs by path. Access is gated per-capability, not per-app: Publications requires separate account-manager enablement on top of the API capability. Schema Contracts exist because every site defines its own objects/fields/APINames, so one fixed toolkit cannot be shipped across tenants.

one_liner.evidence_snippet: Sherlock: Find Usernames Across Social Networks

api_surface.evidence_snippet: If you'd rather not install directly to your system, you can import the module at runtime with -m.

notes: Not a hosted service. Callable via sandboxed execution, not an API. No auth of its own; the real blocker is being blocked by the third-party sites it queries unauthenticated, which is why --tor and --proxy ship built in with a 60s default timeout. Output is text/CSV/XLSX files rather than structured stdout, so a wrapper must parse files. ToS consideration: this is account enumeration, which is a product decision as much as a technical one.

auth_methods.evidence_snippet: You can create a personal access token, generate a token with a GitHub App, or use the built-in GITHUB_TOKEN in a GitHub Actions workflow.

access_tier.evidence_snippet: If you want to use the GitHub REST API for personal use, you can create a personal access token.

api_surface.evidence_snippet: GitHub provides two APIs: a REST API and a GraphQL API.

notes: Multiple simultaneous auth paths: PAT (fine-grained or classic), GitHub App installation token, GITHUB_TOKEN in Actions, OAuth app token, and basic auth (client_id:client_secret) for a narrow set of app-management endpoints. Documents an explicit negative: username/password is not supported. SAML SSO orgs require separate token authorization for classic PATs, which is an org-level gate on top of self-serve credentials. NOTE: mcp marked not_found because the two pages read did not mention one; excluded from mcp scoring rather than counted as a miss.

mcp.evidence_snippet: The Stripe Model Context Protocol (MCP) server provides a set of tools that AI agents can use to interact with the Stripe API and search our knowledge base

notes: Control app for the gold set: if the agent gets Stripe wrong, something is structurally broken. Restricted API keys are a scoped variant of api_key, not a separate auth method. Test keys work immediately with no card and no approval. MCP is marked 'Public preview' on the docs page — the schema captures capability (full) but not stability, which is a real enum limitation. Stripe's docs also ship 'Copy for LLM' and 'View as Markdown' affordances, i.e. some vendors are already publishing agent-readable documentation. The agent missed this MCP entirely because /mcp is a separate docs section not linked from the API reference — same root cause as Twenty, where MCP lived on a marketing page.

api_surface.evidence_snippet: Both are available as REST and GraphQL.

mcp.evidence_snippet: Every Cloud workspace ships with a native MCP server.

notes: Only self-hostable app in the 100, and it is BOTH cloud and self-hosted: base URL is api.twenty.com for cloud, {your-domain} for self-hosted. Schema forces one instance_model value, which is a real limitation. MCP is documented as shipping with Cloud workspaces only, so the self-hosted capability is unverified. Metadata API allows programmatic schema changes (objects, fields, relations) — same toolkit-stability problem as DealCloud Schema Contracts, reached by a different mechanism. MCP evidence lives on a marketing page, not in developer docs.

access_tier.evidence_snippet: Before you can use your app in a production capacity, you must create and configure your own webhook endpoint on a public server

notes: A temporary dashboard token works instantly for testing, but production requires business verification, a registered phone number, message template approval, and a public webhook endpoint. Test credential is not a working credential — that gap is the finding and it is what separates app_review from partner_gated here. Trap noted during hand research: WhatsApp 'authentication templates' are OTP message templates sent to end users, not API authentication.

access_tier.evidence_snippet: Fill out a form and we'll see if a free trial might be right for you.

notes: No public developer documentation found. Shipped products are end-user tools (Excel plugin, Chrome extension, PowerPoint add-in) that require platform login, not a programmatic API. The research set hint mentions a research API; no public docs for it were located. Per the brief, a gated app documented with evidence is a correct finding, not a failure. Free trial is request-and-review, which fails the self-serve test: someone decides whether you get access.
